finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF: the /fetch handler passes the user-supplied `target` query parameter straight to http.Get with no scheme, host, or IP validation. It returns the full response body to the caller. An attacker can reach internal services, cloud metadata (169.254.169.254), and localhost, and read the responses.
finding.sink: http.Get(target) at main.go:16, with the body echoed back via io.Copy at main.go:22

trace.note: http.HandleFunc("/fetch", fetch) registers the route with no auth middleware
target is read from the query string without validation
http.Get(target) issues the outbound request; redirects are followed by default
the response body is copied to the client, so this is full-read SSRF

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, scheme check, IP or private-range block, custom http.Client, or auth on this path. The `allowed` map at main.go:9 is used only by safeFetch, not by fetch.

verdict.reason: main.go:15 reads the attacker-controlled `target` query parameter and passes it unvalidated to http.Get at main.go:16, and main.go:22 echoes the body back. The route is registered at main.go:41 with no auth, and the `allowed` check at main.go:27 applies only to safeFetch.
